summary: Body organization and the structures and processes behind support, movement, nervous signaling and the senses.

topics.title: Anatomical language and homeostasis
topics.description: Directional terms, body planes and levels of organization provide a common way to describe the body. Homeostasis concerns how feedback helps regulate internal conditions.

topics.title: Chemistry, cells and membranes
topics.description: Chemical bonds, water and cell structures connect basic chemistry with living tissue. Membrane transport includes the movement of water and dissolved substances into and out of cells.

topics.title: Tissues, skin and bone
topics.description: The four major tissue types connect microscopic structure with function. Skin layers and bone formation, breakdown and maintenance introduce the body's protective and supporting structures.

topics.title: Muscle structure and contraction
topics.description: Skeletal muscle links a nerve signal with calcium release and interactions between actin and myosin. The topic connects muscle organization with contraction and the role of ATP.

topics.title: Neurons and reflexes
topics.description: Neuron structure, electrical signals and action potentials explain how information travels. Reflex pathways connect sensory input, spinal processing and a motor response.

topics.title: Brain, autonomic control and special senses
topics.description: Brain regions and the autonomic nervous system connect nervous structures with automatic body control. Special senses include the structures and receptors involved in vision and hearing.

sourceNote: Saved Fall 2022 lecture syllabus preview and its stated topic list; accompanying readiness questions follow those lecture outcomes.

summary: Practical identification of anatomical structures, from cells and tissues to the skeleton, muscles and nervous system.

topics.title: Orientation, microscopy and cells
topics.description: Body cavities, directional language and anatomical planes establish orientation. Microscope use and cell identification connect visible structures with their names and functions.

topics.title: Tissues and membranes
topics.description: Recognizing epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue through their structural features. Tissue organization is related to the role of the tissue in a body location.

topics.title: Skin and the skeleton
topics.description: Identification of skin layers and associated structures, followed by the axial and appendicular skeleton. Bone names and distinguishing features provide the basis for locating structures on models.

topics.title: Joints and movements
topics.description: Joint types are connected with movements such as flexion, extension, abduction and adduction. The material relates the structure of a joint to the movements it permits.

topics.title: Gross muscles
topics.description: Locating major muscles and connecting them with the movements they produce. Opposing muscle actions help organize the identification work.

topics.title: Nervous-system structures
topics.description: Nervous tissue, spinal cord, nerves, reflexes, brain regions and cranial nerves form the final practical group. The syllabus also includes autonomic nervous-system structures.

summary: Chemical measurement and atomic structure lead into reactions, quantitative calculations, bonding, gases and solutions.

topics.title: Measurement and chemical amounts
topics.description: Units, significant figures and density support quantitative chemical work. Formula masses and the mole connect measured masses with amounts of substances.

topics.title: Atoms, ions and electron configurations
topics.description: Atomic particles, isotopes and ions establish the structure and charge of an atom. Electron configurations describe the arrangement of its electrons.

topics.title: Formulas, names and reactions
topics.description: Chemical nomenclature connects compound names with formulas. The syllabus also includes empirical formulas, balanced reactions and oxidation–reduction reactions.

topics.title: Stoichiometry and energy
topics.description: Stoichiometry uses a balanced reaction to calculate how much reactant is needed or product can form. Energy calculations relate chemical change to heat and temperature change.

topics.title: Bonding, molecular shapes and attractions
topics.description: Lewis structures and molecular geometry connect the arrangement of atoms with molecular polarity. Intermolecular attractions distinguish interactions between molecules from bonds within a molecule.

topics.title: Gases and solutions
topics.description: Gas relationships connect pressure, volume, temperature and amount. Solution calculations cover concentration and the amount of dissolved substance in a given volume.

sourceNote: Saved Fall 2023 syllabus and Canvas module scope, chapters 1–11; the later modules emphasize gases, intermolecular forces and solutions.

summary: Laboratory measurements, chemical identification and reaction calculations, followed by heat measurements and molecular structures.

topics.title: Measurements, instruments and density
topics.description: Unit conversions, significant figures and instrument readings support reliable measurements. Mass and displaced volume are combined to calculate density.

topics.title: Spectra, elements and electrons
topics.description: Line spectra are compared with reference information to identify elements. Electron configurations and compound naming connect these observations with atomic and ionic descriptions.

topics.title: Reactions and ionic equations
topics.description: Observable reaction changes lead into double-displacement reactions and solubility. Molecular, complete ionic and net ionic equations describe the same reaction at different levels.

topics.title: Composition and reaction yields
topics.description: Mass, mole and particle conversions support empirical-formula and composition calculations. Stoichiometry then connects reaction amounts with theoretical and percentage yields.

topics.title: Calorimetry and specific heat
topics.description: Calorimetry uses measured temperature changes to determine heat exchanged. Specific-heat calculations connect that heat with the sample's mass and temperature change.

topics.title: Lewis structures and molecular geometry
topics.description: Bonding regions and lone pairs are counted around a central atom. Their arrangement is used to distinguish electron-group geometry from molecular shape.

summary: Physical, cognitive and social development across the lifespan, from prenatal development through later life.

topics.title: Developmental theories and research
topics.description: Theories provide different accounts of how people change over time. Research designs distinguish age-related change from differences between generations or groups.

topics.title: Prenatal development and infancy
topics.description: Prenatal periods, birth and early physical development introduce the beginning of the lifespan. Infant cognition and attachment connect early abilities with caregiving relationships.

topics.title: Childhood cognition and relationships
topics.description: Language, thinking and learning develop within family, school and cultural settings. Parenting, temperament and social support help organize the course's treatment of childhood.

topics.title: Adolescence and identity
topics.description: Puberty, changing reasoning and peer relationships are considered together. Identity development includes exploring possibilities and making commitments.

topics.title: Adult roles and midlife
topics.description: Adult development includes work, partnerships, parenting and changing social roles. Midlife topics connect personal development with contributions to other people and future generations.

topics.title: Aging, death and bereavement
topics.description: Later-life material covers physical aging, cognition and social development. Death, grief and mourning are considered within their personal and cultural contexts.
